AGIBOT launches G2 Max with a 40 kg rated dual-arm payload

The robot combines picking, transport and placement, with reported warehouse results and component feeding on a Qiyuan T1 assembly line.

PEdaily ↗26 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Rated and peak loads differ

Launched on October 26, G2 Max is rated for 20 kg per arm or 40 kg across both arms; 50 kg is a peak figure. AGIBOT specifies arm repeatability within ±0.5 mm. This is not a guarantee of end-to-end task accuracy after perception and mobile-base errors.

Results in a specified warehouse setting

The system combines force-controlled arms and vision for differently shaped materials. In the cited e-commerce warehouse setting, AGIBOT reports 80 boxes per hour depalletizing, 75 palletizing and over 99% task success. Those figures describe that setting, not every warehouse.

Feeding production across shifts

AGIBOT also describes joint-component transport on Huguang’s Qiyuan T1 line. Dual hot-swappable batteries, autonomous recharging and Genie Studio 2.0 support sustained work. Safety hardware includes lidar, ultrasound, contact edges and emergency stops; comprehensive certification results, pricing and customer delivery schedules are not specified.
